Firmware checks read a LEXICON_FIRMWARE folder with one subfolder per set and skip when it is absent. The web demo does ship program-name and slider-value catalogs keyed to specific firmware sets.

make check runs the firmware-free checks, and any target whose tool is missing, such as Verilator 5 or KiCad’s command-line tool, reports itself as skipped. The page builds with Emscripten 5.0.1 for GitHub Pages. The plugin builds with CMake and JUCE 8.0.14 as macOS AU, VST3 and standalone targets, and CI validates the AU with auval; the tagged v0.1.0-alpha.1 prerelease is an ad-hoc signed macOS 11+ build that contains no firmware.

make check-firmware runs the user’s ROMs through several layers, including service-manual signature tables at gate level. Qualification compares the emulator’s CPU state, control-store writes and DAC captures with board-level runs, and qualified.json stores expected hashes for two scenarios. A byte-exact gate compares the WebAssembly build bit for bit with the native reference. These project checks need the ROMs.

GitHub detects no repository license, so no reuse terms beyond viewing are granted; the included 8080 cores carry zlib and MIT notices. README disclaims affiliation with Lexicon or its owners, and the original firmware remains theirs. In the Hacker News thread for a related report, a commenter who identifies the repository as theirs describes paid schematic tracing and LLM agents turning schematics into Verilog.

name: Sonic Advance 3: an AI-assisted match of one enemy module
description_en: Macabeus’s dated study describes prompting Claude Sonnet 3.5 and DeepSeek R1 with assembly, similar decompiled functions and structs to write matching C for Marun, one enemy module of the community Sonic Advance 3 GBA decompilation. The resulting pull request replaced that module’s assembly and was merged; the author calls the setting unusually AI-friendly, and the project now bars LLM-origin contributions.
description_zh: Macabeus 在注明日期的研究文章中，介绍了如何把汇编、相似的已反编译函数和结构体放进提示词，让 Claude Sonnet 3.5 与 DeepSeek R1 为社区 Sonic Advance 3 GBA 反编译项目中的敌人模块 Marun 编写匹配的 C 代码。由此产生的拉取请求替换了该模块的汇编并已合并；作者认为这一场景对 AI 格外友好，而该项目现已不接受源自大模型的贡献。
requirements: The post, dated 20 May 2025 and subtitled an ongoing study, covers a single module: Marun, an enemy in the community Sonic Advance 3 GBA matching decompilation. Work began on 6 January 2025, and pull request #4, which replaced the module’s 1,154-line assembly file with 494 lines of C, was merged on 31 January; the post equates it to 0.3% of the project’s total progress. It is a bounded contribution study, not a whole-game decompilation.

Building the SA3 decompilation requires the user’s own European Sonic Advance 3 ROM, named baserom_sa3.gba and matching the release the README identifies by SHA1, plus a sufficiently recent agbcc compiler fork. The study itself worked in decomp.me scratches, putting assembly, similar decompiled functions and relevant structs into prompts for Claude Sonnet 3.5 and DeepSeek R1.

Match percentages come from decomp.me: the post reports a 96% first Sonnet 3.5 attempt that later prompts could not reproduce, a 74% DeepSeek R1 result raised to 100% by replacing memset with CpuFill16, and R1 output that usually matched at least about 60%. The merged pull request is the project-level outcome; the post reports no separate build or test.

The author calls the setting very AI-friendly because similar modules were already decompiled for use as examples and the GBA compiler is simpler and more predictable; generated C lacked project-specific macros and needed readability work. The author’s decomp.me AI-panel pull request was closed unmerged; the post says user benefit was unclear and it required a paid API key.

At the reviewed SA3 commit, the README states a strict no-LLM/no-AI policy for issues and pull requests, so that project no longer accepts this workflow. The SA3 repository has no license file at that commit, and the ROM and its assets retain their own rights.

name: iX500 Scan: a macOS client for the reverse-engineered ScanSnap Wi-Fi protocol
description_en: Replaces ScanSnap Home for a Fujitsu/PFU ScanSnap iX500 on macOS with a SwiftUI app and Python service that scan over Wi-Fi through the community-reverse-engineered VENS protocol, or over USB through SANE, and produce searchable PDFs. It vendors bramheerink’s GPL-2.0 driver, extends it for macOS, and documents further handshake and hardware-status fields, including the scan-button bit. Results are author-reported; the repository publishes no tests or captures.
description_zh: 在 macOS 上以 SwiftUI 应用和 Python 后台服务替代 ScanSnap Home，为富士通／PFU ScanSnap iX500 提供扫描：Wi-Fi 经由社区逆向的 VENS 协议，USB 经由 SANE，输出可搜索的 PDF。项目内置 bramheerink 的 GPL-2.0 驱动并为 macOS 做了扩展，还记录了更多握手字段和硬件状态字段，包括扫描键状态位。结果均为作者报告，仓库未公开测试或抓包记录。
requirements: Reviewed commit 24a5f7c (three commits, all dated 2026-10-15) targets the Fujitsu/PFU ScanSnap iX500. README says ScanSnap Home 3.7 is no longer maintained and hangs on macOS 27; the project offers Wi-Fi scanning started by the device’s scan button, a USB path through SANE, and searchable PDFs with rotation, cropping, blank-page removal and OCR. No release build is published, and other ScanSnap models are not claimed.

The Wi-Fi path needs the user’s own iX500 and two values that README says only ScanSnap Home knows: the scanner’s 12-character pairing key and the paired computer’s 8-byte HostID. They are obtained once from ScanSnap Home’s own connection to that scanner; the repository includes no vendor software, firmware or captures.

Building needs macOS 14+, Xcode 15+ (Swift tools 5.10), the system Python 3 with Pillow, and Homebrew sane-backends, ocrmypdf, img2pdf and tesseract-lang. build.sh bundles the Python service and vendored driver into an ad-hoc-signed app that runs the service with /usr/bin/python3.

The protocol work extends bramheerink/scansnap, whose VENS specification says it was reverse-engineered from captures of ScanSnap Home talking to an iX500. README adds handshake fields for the paired HostID, local time and UTC offset, hardware-status bits for an empty feeder and the scan button, and a session timeout of about 40 s, and notes that Wi-Fi images always arrive as 300 dpi colour, rotated 180° with scanner background. No automated tests, captures or comparisons with ScanSnap Home output are published.

GPL-2.0, matching the vendored driver at commit 5706688, whose file header records the author’s changes. This is an unofficial client, not recovered vendor source or firmware. The repository’s draft social posts credit an evening with Claude Code for closing the remaining protocol gaps.

name: Roborock Local Server: a self-hosted stand-in for Roborock’s vacuum cloud
description_en: Runs a local HTTPS and MQTT stack in place of Roborock’s cloud, so supported vacuums keep live maps and controls on an isolated network without rooting or hardware changes. The maintainer’s technical write-up recounts earlier app and traffic analysis and a later investigation in which Claude Code and Codex worked against an emulated firmware environment. Compatibility is reported per model by the project and its users.
description_zh: 运行一套本地 HTTPS 与 MQTT 服务来替代 Roborock 云端，使受支持的扫地机在隔离网络中无需 root 或改装硬件即可保留实时地图与控制。维护者的技术说明回顾了早期的应用与流量分析，以及后来借助 Claude Code 和 Codex、在模拟固件环境中开展的调查。兼容性由项目及其用户按型号报告。
requirements: Reviewed version 1.2.1 (commit c3b3284) targets most Roborock vacuums on the v2 protocol; README excludes the entry-level Q series, and the tested-models page lists confirmed models, unresolved failures and certificate-chain notes. Documented limitations include firmware updates and schedules; camera streaming is verified on two models, and China-market devices reject commands outside China.

Setup needs a domain the user controls with local DNS rewriting, a valid TLS certificate, a LAN host for Docker Compose or the Home Assistant add-on, and a second Wi-Fi computer for one-time onboarding. The official Roborock app works only after an interception login step and, on Android, a patched APK; Home Assistant and the open-source LocalRock app are alternatives.

Python 3.11–3.13 with FastAPI, aiohttp, cryptography and python-roborock 4.20.0; a container image is published, and CI runs the pytest suite before building it. Tests cover onboarding, protocol authentication, MQTT proxying, certificates and scenes.

The write-up says long-running Claude Code (Opus 4.6) and Codex sessions, given the maintainer’s own rooted S7, its firmware, python-roborock and the decompiled app, helped find the remaining onboarding step after earlier manual attempts stalled. It credits Dennis Giese’s firmware research, Valetudo and other community work.
MIT license with an as-is disclaimer; the project is not affiliated with Roborock. It is a compatible server, not recovered Roborock server code, and vendor firmware or app changes may break it.

name: WristBeam: reconstructing Garmin’s watch protocol for a Mac companion
description_en: Implements a Garmin watch companion as a native macOS menu-bar app that pairs over Bluetooth, receives live health notifications and original FIT files, and can upload them to Garmin Connect. Source comments attribute its GFDI framing, handshake, file-transfer and status fields to analysis of a supplied Garmin Android package, cross-checked against community implementations such as Gadgetbridge. Device verification covers one watch model, and the opt-in MCP and HTTP interfaces expose only locally cached data.
description_zh: 以原生 macOS 菜单栏应用实现佳明手表的配套客户端：通过蓝牙配对，接收实时健康通知和原始 FIT 文件，并可上传至 Garmin Connect。源码注释称，GFDI 分帧、握手、文件传输和状态字段依据对一个自备佳明 Android 安装包的分析实现，并与 Gadgetbridge 等社区实现相互核对。设备验证仅涵盖一款手表；可选启用的 MCP 与 HTTP 接口只提供本地缓存的数据。
requirements: Reviewed at VERSION 0.3.7 plus unreleased changes. It needs macOS 13+, a Garmin watch prepared with heart-rate broadcast off, and, for cloud features, a Garmin China or Global account signed in through Garmin’s own page; a local mode pauses all Garmin cloud access. Application-level encryption, native MLR/CoreTransfer and desktop widgets are unsupported, and a sleeping Mac cannot sync.

Protocol source comments describe an independent Swift implementation of GFDI framing (COBS, CRC-16), multilink registration, device information, file directories and transfers, battery status and account-identity fields, each tied to named classes of a supplied Garmin Android package. Gadgetbridge, garmin-bridge and garmin-ble are cited as corroborating wire observations that were consulted, not ported. The reviewed tree contains no APK or decompiled listing; cloud history uses Connect client endpoints that the developer guide says are not a published Garmin API contract.

Building needs macOS 13+, Swift 5.9+ and Command Line Tools; native swift test and CodeQL analysis need full Xcode, which CI supplies. CONTRIBUTING lists lint, localization, secret-scan, release-pipeline and core regression scripts. Release packages are ad hoc signed and not Apple notarized.

The device matrix marks pairing, fresh notifications, original FIT download, China upload and daily charts verified only for an Instinct 2 Solar on 2026-10-13, with firmware unrecorded. Other Instinct, fēnix, epix, Forerunner, Venu and vívoactive models and real Global uploads remain unverified. VERIFICATION.md records regression counts run through Command Line Tools rather than full XCTest.

MIT covers the project, which says it is not affiliated with Garmin; Garmin services, the Android package, watch firmware and health data keep their own terms. MCP, the HTTP/HTTPS API and webhooks are off until enabled.

name: abc-decompiler
description_en: Decompiler for HarmonyOS Ark bytecode (.abc), the format HarmonyOS app packages carry in modules.abc, built by adapting the jadx decompiler and reading files through a patched copy of the abcde library. Because much of Ark bytecode is semantically close to DEX, it reuses jadx's GUI, IR and passes: an .abc file dropped into the jadx-based window is shown as decompiled code. The README reports that all 227 usable instructions of the 282 Ark opcodes are implemented, most special instructions as pseudo-functions.
description_zh: 面向鸿蒙方舟字节码（.abc）的反编译工具；HarmonyOS 应用包中的 modules.abc 即为此格式。它通过改造 jadx 反编译器实现，并借助打过补丁的 abcde 库读取文件。由于方舟字节码有很大一部分与 DEX 字节码语义相近，它沿用了 jadx 的图形界面、中间表示和处理流程：把 .abc 文件拖入基于 jadx 的窗口即可查看反编译代码。README 称 282 条方舟字节码中可用的 227 条指令均已实现，其中大部分特殊指令以伪函数形式实现。
requirements: The README describes the project as still in development: decompilation passes for more readable output, a custom IR and data-flow analysis are listed as unfinished. The only release, h1, published 2024-12-20, ships a single jadx-dev-all.jar built from the reviewed master commit, and the repository has had no pushes since.

Building needs JDK 17+; the patched abcde fork must first be published to the local Maven repository and its version substituted into the Gradle files before ./gradlew dist. Input is the modules.abc file from the user's own HarmonyOS HAP package.

The repository is a modified jadx code base: jadx's DEX input, test samples and inherited CI files remain, and it has no GitHub Actions workflow of its own, so no tests of Ark bytecode output are reported.
Apache-2.0, as inherited from jadx; the abcde fork is also Apache-2.0.

name: pypush: a Python client for Apple’s push protocol
description_en: Reimplements the client side of Apple’s private Apple Push Notification service (APNs) protocol in platform-independent Python: it activates as an Apple device, connects to the APNs courier, mints app-scoped tokens and receives push notifications. The project began as the author’s proof of concept for iMessage reverse engineering, but the current rewrite has removed IDS and iMessage support for now. It uses Apple’s services outside Apple’s official clients.
description_zh: 以与平台无关的 Python 重新实现 Apple 私有推送通知服务（APNs）协议的客户端：它以 Apple 设备身份完成激活，连接 APNs courier 服务器，生成限定于应用的令牌并接收推送通知。项目最初是作者 iMessage 逆向研究的概念验证，但当前重写版暂时移除了 IDS 和 iMessage 支持。它在 Apple 官方客户端之外使用 Apple 的服务。
requirements: Reviewed at the 2026-03-15 main head, identical to release v2.0.2 on PyPI. The README warns that the rewrite is unstable, that many features have been temporarily removed and that stability should not be expected before 3.0.0. The IDS, iMessage, GrandSlam and CloudKit packages are empty placeholders, so the earlier iMessage work is not part of this version.

Activation and connections go to Apple’s live activation and APNs servers through what the project calls Apple’s internal API, outside Apple’s official clients; the README notes that some APIs may need device identifiers. Apple’s terms for these services apply separately.

Requires Python 3.9+ with anyio, httpx (HTTP/2) and cryptography; the cli extra adds Frida, Rich and Typer. The CLI listens for notifications on a topic, and its proxy mode, meant for observing a Mac’s own APNs traffic, attaches Frida to the local apsd daemon and requires System Integrity Protection disabled and root.

Pull-request CI runs Ruff and pytest on Python 3.9–3.12 across Linux, macOS and Windows. The tests activate against Apple’s servers, open an APNs connection and round-trip a sandbox notification through a scoped token, so they depend on live services rather than offline protocol fixtures.
LICENSE is the Server Side Public License v1, and the package metadata classifies it as Other/Proprietary; the README says Beeper purchased the project and directs licensing questions to Beeper.

name: LuaJIT Decompiler v2
description_en: Decompiles LuaJIT bytecode files back into Lua source, written as a replacement for the older Python LuaJIT decompiler. The README reports full support for gotos and for stripped bytecode, including reconstructed locals and upvalues, and its boolean-expression recovery follows a published decompilation algorithm. It processes single files or whole folders and writes .lua output.
description_zh: 将 LuaJIT 字节码文件反编译回 Lua 源码，作为旧版 Python LuaJIT 反编译器的替代品编写。README 称它完整支持 goto 和去除调试信息的字节码，包括还原局部变量和上值；其布尔表达式恢复基于一篇已发表的反编译算法论文。它可处理单个文件或整个文件夹，输出 .lua 文件。
requirements: Users supply LuaJIT bytecode files or a folder containing them, by drag and drop or on the command line; decompiled .lua files go to an output folder beside the executable unless overridden. Options filter by extension, ignore debug info, skip files that fail instead of showing an assertion pop-up, and format output to minimize diffs.

The reader accepts bytecode format versions 1 and 2 and rejects big-endian bytecode, which the README lists as future work along with better decompilation of conditional assignments. The repository has no tests, CI or published accuracy results; the program reports how many files failed to decompile.

Windows only: the README directs users to a release executable (the Mar_24_2024 release, whose notes say it was rebuilt on 2026-05-14), and main.h lists Visual Studio, C++20, the Windows API and an unsigned default char as build requirements, with no project or build files included. A Call-of-Duty branch, four commits ahead of master, has its own release executable. Last commit at review: 2026-05-14.
MIT license text that also carries the LuaJIT and Lua copyright notices; GitHub does not classify it.

name: FLARE Learning Hub
description_en: Free English reverse-engineering and malware-analysis modules from Mandiant's FLARE team, published as Google Docs, with lab binaries, IDA databases and scripts kept in this repository. The Malware Analysis Crash Course builds from x86 basics to reading Windows API use through assembly-patching exercises and labs with worked solutions; the other modules introduce WinDbg Time Travel Debugging for malware triage and provide a reference to how Go 1.24 programs look in Windows executables.
description_zh: Mandiant FLARE 团队发布的免费英文逆向工程与恶意软件分析课程模块，正文以 Google Docs 形式发布，实验用二进制文件、IDA 数据库和脚本存放在本仓库中。其中的恶意软件分析速成课从 x86 基础讲到解读 Windows API 调用，穿插汇编修改练习和附详细解答的实验；其余模块介绍如何用 WinDbg 时间旅行调试（Time Travel Debugging）分诊恶意软件，并提供一份说明 Go 1.24 程序在 Windows 可执行文件中呈现方式的参考手册。
requirements: At reviewed commit ebd4e3a (2026-03-31), the repository, first committed on 2026-03-19, holds three modules: Malware Analysis Crash Course (nine chapters, five labs, hacking exercises and flash quizzes), An Introduction to Time Travel Debugging (a demo, one triage lab and a JavaScript automation reference) and The Go Reverse Engineering Reference. Module text lives in web-published Google Docs that change outside the repository. The README promises refinements and new modules, but no commits followed 31 March by the review date.

The crash course is the entry point: it assumes Windows command-line use, Boolean logic, two's complement, basic programming and networking. The TTD module assumes basic x86 Windows reversing and WinDbg. The Go reference assumes x86 reversing and Go, and is restricted to Windows AMD64 executables built with Go 1.24.0.

The README says all modules support only Intel x86-64 environments and strongly recommends an isolated, snapshot-capable FLARE-VM virtual machine. The crash course uses IDA and FakeNet, and its exercises ship with IDA database files; the TTD module uses WinDbg, which includes TTD, and ttd.exe. Lab and demo binaries, databases and scripts are FLARE-made and come as password-protected archives. The README warns that some behave like malware and may be flagged, so they belong only in that VM; one TTD demo trace is a separate Google Drive download.
The repository is Apache-2.0; the Google Docs reviewed carry no separate license statement. The project does not accept contributions and takes errata by email.

name: pw: a matching decompilation of the Pokéwalker firmware
description_en: Reconstructs as C the firmware of the Pokéwalker, the pedometer accessory for Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver, for its Renesas H8/38606 microcontroller. With artwork from the user’s retail firmware image and a supported Renesas compiler suite, the README reports a byte-identical rebuild of the 48 KiB image; without that image, original placeholder art gives a non-matching reference build. The author describes disassembling and decompiling the retail binary, the HeartGold/SoulSilver ROMs and the candidate compilers, alongside published hardware research.
description_zh: 以 C 语言重建 Pokéwalker 的固件。Pokéwalker 是《宝可梦 心金／魂银》配套的计步器配件，采用 Renesas H8/38606 微控制器。README 报告，使用从使用者自备的零售固件镜像中取得的美术素材及受支持的 Renesas 编译器套件，可重新构建出逐字节相同的 48 KiB 镜像；没有该镜像时，项目原创的占位美术只能生成不一致的参考构建。作者称其结合已公开的硬件研究，对零售二进制文件、心金／魂银 ROM 及候选编译器进行了反汇编和反编译。
requirements: The reviewed main branch is a single initial-release commit of 2026-09-14 with no tags or releases. The README calls the matching reconstruction complete for one image, 49,152 bytes with SHA-256 f9e210a3…d15607, and assumes it is the only Pokéwalker firmware. The source keeps 40 C90 modules whose file names encode the observed link order, and changes must preserve matching.

Users supply a lawfully obtained Pokéwalker firmware image, used only for artwork, and the Renesas H8, H8S, H8SX family C compiler package; neither is distributed, and the README withholds acquisition instructions. Only suites 6.02.01 and 6.02.02 are reported to reproduce the image. Missing artwork falls back to the bundled placeholders, which normally changes the output hash.

Builds are reported on macOS Arm64, where the 32-bit Windows compiler runs through Wibo and Rosetta, and natively on Windows x86_64; other hosts are unverified. uv supplies Python 3.11+ (3.12 by default), Ninja and Pillow from uv.lock, configure.py generates build.ninja, and macOS configuration downloads and validates the recorded Wibo release.

ninja verify requires the retail size and SHA-256 and writes verified.json; the build guide asks for that check under both compiler suites and records per-module input and output hashes to catch stale objects. Host unit tests cover the build utilities, a development check adds clang-format, Ruff and Cppcheck, and there is no CI workflow. Matching is author-reported.

Original project material is dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0, and the placeholder artwork carries its own CC0 notice; retail firmware and extracted artwork keep their rights. include/startup/iodefine.h is a retained Renesas HEW device header outside the CC0 dedication with no license grant, and the compiler-archive reader credits MIT-licensed ISx and Unshield. The project states no affiliation with Nintendo, The Pokémon Company, GAME FREAK or Renesas.

name: slicer
description_en: Browser-based Java reverse-engineering tool that loads class files and JAR/ZIP archives and disassembles or decompiles them with Vineflower (the default), CFR, Procyon or JASM, compiled to run in the browser, next to its own bytecode disassembler. It draws inheritance and interface graphs and per-method control-flow graphs, searches constant-pool entries, instructions and member declarations or usages, applies Tiny, SRG/TSRG/CSRG or ProGuard mappings, and offers generic transformers that strip or normalize bytecode attributes so decompilers cope better with obfuscation. A JavaScript scripting API can add disassemblers and manipulate the workspace; the README itself recommends Recaf for serious reverse engineering.
description_zh: 基于浏览器的 Java 逆向工程工具：可加载 class 文件和 JAR/ZIP 归档，使用编译为可在浏览器中运行的 Vineflower（默认）、CFR、Procyon 或 JASM 进行反汇编或反编译，另有自带的字节码反汇编器。它能绘制继承与接口实现关系图以及单个方法的控制流图，搜索常量池条目、指令以及成员声明或使用位置，可应用 Tiny、SRG/TSRG/CSRG 或 ProGuard 映射，还提供剥离或规范化字节码属性的通用转换器，帮助反编译器更好地应对混淆。JavaScript 脚本 API 可添加反汇编器并操作工作区；README 自己也建议，若要进行严肃的逆向工程，应使用 Recaf。
requirements: Runs as the hosted web app at slicer.run and can be installed as a PWA. The repository has no releases or tags, so this entry pins the reviewed main commit (2026-09-19); local builds are a Vite and Svelte app built with pnpm, and the repository has no CI workflow. The documentation says slicer is in active development and that features may be missing.

The documentation states that no data is sent to any server and that decompilers run locally in the browser; JDK library classes are fetched on demand from data.slicer.run, and URL parameters can load a JAR, mapping file or script from another site. Input is class files or JAR/ZIP archives from software the user may analyze; HPROF heap dumps and Android binary XML can also be viewed.

The documentation warns that decompiled output is a best-effort approximation that may not be valid Java, especially for code from non-javac compilers or obfuscators. slicer has no obfuscator-specific deobfuscation, and its remapper does not propagate names through inheritance.
MIT license for slicer; bundled components such as the Vineflower and Procyon decompilers are Apache-2.0.

name: SteamKit
description_en: .NET library that implements the client side of Valve’s Steam network protocol: connection-manager sessions, authentication, friends, unified service and Game Coordinator messages, Web API calls and CDN depot downloads. Message classes are generated from Steam protobufs tracked in a submodule and from the project’s own SteamLanguage definitions. Its Resources tree adds protocol-research tools: NetHook2, a Windows DLL that hooks a running Steam client to dump the network messages it exchanges, NetHookAnalyzer2 for viewing those dumps, and ProtobufDumper for recovering protobuf definitions from executables.
description_zh: 实现 Valve Steam 网络协议客户端的 .NET 库，涵盖连接管理服务器会话、身份验证、好友、统一服务消息与 Game Coordinator 消息、Web API 调用以及 CDN depot 下载。消息类由子模块跟踪的 Steam protobuf 和项目自有的 SteamLanguage 定义生成。其 Resources 目录还提供协议研究工具：NetHook2 是挂钩正在运行的 Steam 客户端、转储其收发网络消息的 Windows DLL，NetHookAnalyzer2 用于查看这些转储，ProtobufDumper 则从可执行文件中恢复 protobuf 定义。
requirements: The reviewed master head is identical to GitHub release 3.5.0 of 2026-10-19; at review NuGet still listed 3.4.0 as the newest SteamKit2 package. The README requires the .NET 10 runtime to use the library and the .NET 10 SDK to build it, although the library project multi-targets net8.0 and net10.0. Documentation consists of XML API docs, the wiki and numbered samples covering login, QR authentication, web cookies, friends, Web API and a Dota Game Coordinator request.

Authenticated features need the user’s own Steam account. The library follows Valve’s undocumented, changing protocol: a weekly workflow regenerates message classes from the SteamTracking protobuf submodule and opens a pull request, and the NetHook2 readme notes that releases can lag behind Steam changes.

NetHook2 is a Windows-only C++ DLL built with Visual Studio 2022 and vcpkg that needs the x86 Visual C++ redistributable. Its readme says it depends on binary signature scans of the Steam client that updates can break, and that Steam may crash while it is attached. NetHookAnalyzer2 is a Windows GUI; CI publishes both as workflow artifacts. They inspect the user’s own client traffic.

CI builds the library, SteamLanguage parser, protobuf tools and samples on Windows, macOS and Linux (x64 and ARM) and runs the xUnit v3 test project, whose fixtures include recorded packets and small depot manifest and chunk samples. The tests check parsing, crypto helpers, async jobs and depot handling, not equivalence with Valve’s client.
LGPL-2.1 (LICENSE). The tracked Steam protobuf definitions come from a separate submodule, and Valve’s services and terms apply independently of the library license.

name: Nintendo Switch Reverse Engineering
description_en: Notes begun by dekuNukem in 2017 and extended by contributors on how the Joy-Con, Pro Controller and parts of the Switch console and dock work, worked out from teardowns, logic-analyzer captures and packet logs. Markdown files cover the Joy-Con board test points and rail-connector pinout, the wired serial handshake with its CRC-8 checksum, Bluetooth HID input and output reports with 32 documented subcommands, the USB HID commands of the Pro Controller and charging grip, the SPI flash memory map with stick and 6-axis calibration, IMU conversion formulas and rumble encoding tables. The repository also keeps STM32 test firmware that plays the console or a Joy-Con on the rail, a Wireshark dissector for the Bluetooth traffic, and the captures behind the notes.
description_zh: 由 dekuNukem 于 2017 年发起、众多贡献者陆续补充的笔记，记录 Joy-Con、Pro 手柄以及 Switch 主机与底座部分硬件的工作方式，依据来自拆机、逻辑分析仪抓取和数据包记录。各 Markdown 文件涵盖 Joy-Con 电路板测试点与滑轨接口引脚定义、带 CRC-8 校验的有线串口握手、蓝牙 HID 输入与输出报告及其中记录的 32 个子命令、Pro 手柄与充电握把的 USB HID 命令、含摇杆与六轴校准数据的 SPI 闪存布局、IMU 换算公式以及振动编码表。仓库还保存了在滑轨接口上扮演主机或 Joy-Con 的 STM32 测试固件、用于解析蓝牙流量的 Wireshark 解析器，以及笔记所依据的抓取数据。
requirements: Reviewed at commit b354f21 (2026-08-21). Of 277 commits, 228 date from 2017 and most others from 2018–2021; the 2026 changes document the console's sanity checks on stick calibration. The notes describe the original Joy-Con and Pro Controller, listing controller firmware 3.89 as the latest, and several fields remain marked unknown, so newer firmware and controllers need separate checking.

Following the notes needs one's own controller. The wired-protocol work involves opening a Joy-Con and connecting its rail connector, which uses 1.8 V logic, to a logic analyzer or microcontroller; the Bluetooth and USB notes assume a host that can exchange raw HID reports, and their sample C code uses hidapi-style calls. No controller or dock firmware is included: the README says a dock firmware dump was made but is not posted.

The joycon_reader and joycon_spoofer projects target an STM32F072 and were generated with STM32CubeMX for Keil MDK-ARM; their build outputs are committed alongside the sources. The nxbt dissector has to be compiled as a plugin within a Wireshark source build, a Lua script dissects Bluetooth traffic captured over USB, and small Python scripts parse captures and compute the serial checksum. The .logicdata captures need logic-analyzer software that reads that format.

The Bluetooth notes also document SPI flash write and sector-erase and firmware-update commands, with warnings about erasing whole sectors; the field meanings come from the contributors' own captures and tests.

GitHub detects no license and the repository has no license file, so the notes state no reuse terms; a datasheets folder holds copies of third-party chip datasheets, and the Lua dissector says it is provided with no license. The README credits the many contributors.

name: Android App Reverse Engineering 101
description_en: Maddie Stone's free English workshop introducing static reverse engineering of Android apps, published as GitHub Pages. Its chapters cover app components and entry points, Dalvik bytecode and smali, decompiling DEX with jadx, finding and reading JNI native libraries in Ghidra, and string deobfuscation. Seven exercises with written solutions apply this to triaging malware samples and spotting command-execution flaws in pre-installed apps.
description_zh: Maddie Stone 编写的免费英文工作坊，以 GitHub Pages 发布，入门讲解 Android 应用的静态逆向工程。各章涵盖应用组件与入口点、Dalvik 字节码与 smali、用 jadx 反编译 DEX、在 Ghidra 中定位并阅读 JNI 原生库，以及字符串去混淆。七个附书面解答的练习将这些方法用于分诊恶意软件样本，以及找出预装应用中的命令执行缺陷。
requirements: Reviewed at commit 17f9eeb, the last default-branch commit (2020-04-29); most pages date from 2019 and the material is not being extended. The introduction says the workshop covers static analysis only and does not teach app development, malware analysis or vulnerability hunting themselves; the conclusion points to Frida and dynamic analysis as next steps.

Exercises are designed for the author's Ubuntu 18.04 64-bit VM image, offered for VirtualBox and VMware from Google Drive, with jadx and Ghidra installed. The exercise APKs (apps triaged as possible malware and two pre-installed vendor apps, each named with a SHA-256 digest in most exercises) exist only inside that VM; the repository holds Markdown pages and images and no APKs.

The native-library chapter assumes some ARM assembly, pointing to outside tutorials, and says every exercise library also has an x86 build. The pages were last updated in 2020, so their screenshots may not match current jadx and Ghidra releases.
The repository has no license file, so reuse terms for the text are not stated; the pages credit the Android robot logo to Google under CC BY 3.0.

name: wii-ipl: a decompilation of the Wii Menu (System Menu 4.3)
description_en: A work-in-progress decompilation of the Wii Menu, the console’s System Menu (IPL), targeting version 4.3 in its USA, European, Japanese and Korean builds. It recovers the menu’s own code together with the Revolution SDK, NintendoWare (NW4R), EGG and middleware libraries linked into it, matched unit by unit against the original executable with decomp-toolkit and objdiff. The repository holds no assets or assembly; a build needs the user’s own Wii Menu WAD and yields only main.dol.
description_zh: Wii Menu（即主机的 System Menu，IPL）的反编译重建，仍在进行中，针对 4.3 版的美、欧、日、韩四个版本。项目重建菜单自身的代码，以及链接进其中的 Revolution SDK、NintendoWare（NW4R）、EGG 和中间件库，并借助 decomp-toolkit 与 objdiff 逐个编译单元与原可执行文件比对。仓库不含任何素材或汇编；构建需要使用者自己的 Wii Menu WAD，且只生成 main.dol。
requirements: The reviewed main commit has no releases or tags. decomp.dev’s report for that commit puts 4.3U at 58.5% matched code, 8,837 of 12,563 functions (70.3%) and 45.2% fully linked code, with the menu’s own code at 53.6% matched; library READMEs mark each RVL_SDK, NW4R, EGG, RevoEX and middleware component as matching, equivalent or not yet matching. The build yields main.dol, not a WAD, and the README warns that the code is not fully shiftable because no SEL file is generated.

Users supply their own Wii Menu 4.3 WAD for the selected version (4.3U by default, or 4.3E, 4.3J or 4.3K); the README states that the repository contains no assets or assembly of the executable. Each version’s configuration pins the SHA-1 of the target main.dol.

Builds need Python and Ninja on Windows, macOS or Linux. configure.py pins decomp-toolkit v1.7.5, objdiff v3.4.5, binutils 2.42-1 and the 20251118 compiler bundle for Metrowerks CodeWarrior (GC/3.0a5.2 as the linker version), and wibo runs the 32-bit Windows tools on macOS and Linux. CONTRIBUTING lists Ghidra with a shared project, IDA/Hex-Rays, m2c and decomp.me as decompiling aids and objdiff for diffing.
CI builds all four versions in a private container that supplies the original files, then uploads map files and progress reports; the percentages above come from those reports.

LICENSE is CC0 1.0. The BTE Bluetooth library notes code taken from Android’s bluedroid under Apache-2.0, and the GameSpy SDK subset is BSD-3-Clause. The decompiled third-party middleware (JustSystems ATOK, Zi eZiText, TMC JPEG, eSOL PrFILE2) and the Opera WWW headers carry no separate grants, and the Wii Menu keeps Nintendo’s rights. CONTRIBUTING forbids using AI to decompile code and asks contributors to avoid AI-only matching forks.

name: usque: an open reimplementation of Cloudflare WARP’s MASQUE mode
description_en: Reimplements the MASQUE mode of Cloudflare’s WARP client in Go, tunnelling IP traffic over QUIC/HTTP/3 with Connect-IP (RFC 9484) and exposing it as a native TUN device, SOCKS5 or HTTP proxies, TCP-only L4 proxies or port forwarding. RESEARCH.md describes how the author worked out device enrollment, TLS client authentication and Cloudflare’s non-standard cf-connect-ip variant by analyzing the official Android client with Frida, mitmproxy, JADX, IDA Free and Wireshark. It registers with and connects to Cloudflare’s service outside the official client.
description_zh: 用 Go 重新实现 Cloudflare WARP 客户端的 MASQUE 模式：通过基于 QUIC/HTTP/3 的 Connect-IP（RFC 9484）隧道传输 IP 流量，并以原生 TUN 设备、SOCKS5 或 HTTP 代理、仅 TCP 的 L4 代理或端口转发等形式提供。RESEARCH.md 记录了作者如何借助 Frida、mitmproxy、JADX、IDA Free 和 Wireshark 分析官方 Android 客户端，弄清设备注册、TLS 客户端认证以及 Cloudflare 非标准的 cf-connect-ip 变体。它在官方客户端之外向 Cloudflare 服务注册并建立连接。
requirements: Reviewed at the 2026-07-20 main head, identical to release v4.2.1. The README calls the project early-stage, says its Go API is unstable if used as a library, and states that only the Linux amd64 release binary was tested, although builds are published for Android, Linux, Windows and macOS on several architectures. RESEARCH.md is a narrative research log; the concise protocol document the README plans has not been written.

Requires access to Cloudflare’s WARP service: the register command creates a new WARP account and enrolls a device key, and the generated config holds that registration’s keys and tokens. The tool uses Cloudflare’s service outside the official client; the README says it is not affiliated with, endorsed by or reviewed by Cloudflare, asks users not to abuse the service and notes that the tool is detectable. ZeroTrust login needs SSO the tool cannot perform.

Building needs Go 1.26.3+ with CGO disabled. The project depends on the author’s fork of connect-ip-go because, the README says, Cloudflare’s implementation is not fully RFC 9484-compliant; quic-go carries the connection, and gVisor and wireguard-go netstacks let the proxy modes run in user space without root. Native TUN mode is limited to Linux and Windows, while the README’s Known Issues list still says Linux only. A Dockerfile is provided.

CI verifies modules and runs go build, go vet, go test and golangci-lint, but the reviewed tree contains no Go test files, so correctness evidence is the author’s own use. The README reports one SOCKS5 speed test of about 834/773 Mbps on a 1 Gbps link and lists missing features such as happy eyeballs, WireGuard and DNS-over-HTTPS. These results are author-reported.
MIT (LICENSE.md). Cloudflare’s service terms and trademarks apply separately, and the README describes usque as an independent research project.

name: awesome-unofficial-pc-ports
description_en: A single-README guide to unofficial PC ports of console games built from decompilations or recompilations and chosen for easy installation by players. Its 76 game entries, grouped under Nintendo, PlayStation, Xbox, SEGA, Indie and J2ME, each recommend a port with short setup notes and often link the underlying decompilation and alternative ports; a Utilities section adds two recompilation launchers.
description_zh: 以单个 README 维护的非官方 PC 移植指南，收录基于反编译或重编译、且便于玩家安装的主机游戏移植。76 个游戏条目按 Nintendo、PlayStation、Xbox、SEGA、独立游戏和 J2ME 分组，每项推荐一个移植版并附简短安装说明，常同时链接所依据的反编译项目和其他移植版；“实用工具”部分另列两个重编译启动器。
requirements: The reviewed README, committed 2026-10-15, has 78 collapsible entries: 43 Nintendo, 12 PlayStation, 14 Xbox, 5 SEGA, 1 indie and 1 J2ME game, plus 2 launcher utilities. Its stated criteria are console games ported to PC through decompilation or recompilation that offer an easy install path, such as a launcher or drag-and-drop; a star marks the most user-friendly option for each game.

Entries are written for players: a recommended port, a line or two of setup notes and, for some games, the underlying decompilation, alternative ports or tutorial videos. They state no matching, completion or license status, and the list also carries projects outside its stated criteria, such as Severed Chains, which it calls a reverse-engineered native recreation, and a port of the PC game Cave Story+.

Most entries tell players to supply their own ROM, disc image, ISO, game dump or XBLA package. The Ratchet & Clank: Clone Home entry also links a third-party archive.org copy of the recovered original J2ME build.

The README promotes Quiver Launcher, a separate catalog website and launcher, and says the list is kept up in spare time with updates that can take months. The repository holds only README.md and an MIT license (copyright 2023 Sebastrion); linked ports, original games and their assets keep their own rights. An independent discovery list.

name: Reverse Engineering iOS Applications
description_en: Ivan Rodriguez's free English course (version 1.1) on reverse engineering iOS applications, aimed at beginners in iOS app security. Five Markdown modules cover setting up a jailbroken test device, decrypting App Store apps for analysis, static analysis of an IPA's files, frameworks, Objective-C classes and ARM binary in Hopper or Ghidra, runtime analysis with Cycript and Frida, and binary patching in Hopper. Exercises use CoinZa, a deliberately insecure Objective-C app the author built from vulnerability classes he reports finding in production App Store apps.
description_zh: Ivan Rodriguez 编写的免费英文课程（1.1 版），讲解 iOS 应用逆向工程，面向 iOS 应用安全初学者。五个 Markdown 模块依次介绍越狱测试设备的环境配置、为分析而解密 App Store 应用、对 IPA 中的文件、框架、Objective-C 类和 ARM 二进制进行静态分析（使用 Hopper 或 Ghidra）、用 Cycript 和 Frida 做运行时分析，以及在 Hopper 中修补二进制。练习使用 CoinZa：作者根据其所述在 App Store 正式应用中发现的漏洞类型，专门编写的一个故意不安全的 Objective-C 应用。
requirements: Reviewed at commit 183873a (2024-04-17). The course was written mainly in 2019; commits since mid-2020 are a few small wording and command fixes. Device instructions cover iOS 10 through 12, and many setup tools are from that period, so they may not work on current devices. The introduction excludes jailbreaking, iOS exploitation, tweak development, backend API testing and in-depth ARM assembly.

The prerequisites page lists no mandatory knowledge but recommends a Mac (Xcode has no Windows alternative), basic Objective-C, Swift, JavaScript, HTML, SSH/SCP and man-in-the-middle concepts, and an ARM disassembler such as Ghidra, IDA or Hopper's trial. A jailbroken iPhone/iPad/iPod on iOS 10 or later is needed only for the decryption module and the Cycript and Frida exercises.

No third-party app is needed for the exercises: the author ships CoinZa as an already-decrypted IPA, plus an EPUB of the course, in the companion repository RE-iOS-Apps-Extras-Github. The README says its vulnerabilities come from production apps but are reproduced in CoinZa instead of being published against those apps, and the closing page asks readers to report vulnerabilities responsibly.

There is no separate license file; the README carries an MIT-style permission notice (Copyright 2019 Ivan Rodriguez) and an at-your-own-risk disclaimer; the closing page asks people who reuse the material to credit the author.

name: Webamp: a browser reimplementation of Winamp 2
description_en: Reimplements Winamp 2's main, equalizer and playlist windows in HTML5 and JavaScript, with Web Audio playback, volume, balance and equalizer, and renders original classic .wsz skins, which its documentation says match Winamp 2.9 pixel for pixel; Milkdrop presets run through the Butterchurn WebGL port. It ships as the webamp npm module for embedding in web pages, and the same monorepo runs webamp.org and the skins.webamp.org skin museum. Its webamp-modern prototype targets Winamp 3/5 modern skins with an interpreter for MAKI skin scripts, whose undocumented bytecode format the author reverse engineered and documents in the repository.
description_zh: 用 HTML5 和 JavaScript 重新实现 Winamp 2 的主窗口、均衡器和播放列表窗口，借助 Web Audio 实现播放、音量、声道平衡和均衡器，并渲染原有的经典 .wsz 皮肤，其文档称渲染效果与 Winamp 2.9 逐像素一致；Milkdrop 预设通过 Butterchurn 的 WebGL 移植版运行。它以 webamp npm 模块的形式发布，可嵌入网页，同一 monorepo 还运行着 webamp.org 和 skins.webamp.org 皮肤博物馆。其中的 webamp-modern 原型面向 Winamp 3/5 的现代皮肤，内含 MAKI 皮肤脚本解释器；MAKI 字节码格式原本没有公开文档，作者对其进行了逆向分析，并在仓库中写成文档。
requirements: Release at review: webamp 2.3.1 on npm, published 2026-06-16; the reviewed master commit (2026-10-17) adds unreleased accessibility and API changes listed in the changelog. The README says it works in modern Edge, Firefox, Safari and Chrome. It reimplements Winamp's behavior and skin rendering rather than recovering Winamp's code, and webamp-modern remains a prototype with an open list of unimplemented MAKI and skin features.

No original Winamp installation is needed: Webamp bundles a default skin and sample track, and users can load their own Winamp 2 .wsz skins, audio files, Milkdrop presets and .eqf equalizer presets. Skins and audio fetched from another domain must be served with CORS permission, because Webamp reads their contents.

Development uses pnpm and Turborepo; .nvmrc names Node.js 22 and CI uses Node.js 20 to build every package, lint, type-check and run the Jest tests. These test Webamp's own parsing and rendering. Compiling webamp-modern's MAKI test scripts calls the bundled Winamp 5.66 mc.exe, directly on Windows or through Wine elsewhere.

The code is MIT-licensed, and the README says the Winamp name, interface and sample audio file are Nullsoft's property. Bundled files that carry no license of their own: the Nullsoft MAKI compiler builds under packages/webamp-modern/resources/maki_compiler (five mc.exe versions from Winamp 3 alpha 8r to Winamp 5.66, nscrt.dll and the MAKI .mi library headers), the skins named after Winamp defaults (base-2.91, Winamp 3 build 499, Winamp Modern 5.66) and the third-party community skins used for demos and tests, the llama sample MP3 and the Winamp Modern Skins tutorial PDF. The bundled Perl MAKI decompiler is GPL-2.0.

name: awesome-decompilation
description_en: A short, link-only reading list on decompiling machine code, last updated in 2023. Its 45 links cover foundational theses, compiler and program-analysis books, decompiler products and projects, pipeline topics from intermediate representations to type, control-flow and identifier recovery, early neural-decompilation papers and binary-to-source matching.
description_zh: 篇幅不长、只列链接的机器码反编译阅读清单，最近一次更新在 2023 年。45 个链接涵盖奠基性学位论文、编译器与程序分析书籍、反编译器产品和项目，从中间表示到类型、控制流和标识符恢复的反编译流程主题，早期神经网络反编译论文，以及二进制与源码匹配。
requirements: Not maintained as a current index: the reviewed master commit of 2023-03-05 is the newest in the repository and added the December 2022 preprint Beyond the C (arXiv 2212.08950). The AI-based section therefore stops at six neural-decompilation papers and projects, and later work, including LLM-based decompilation, is absent.

Entries are bare links under 13 headings, with no annotations, dates, status or license notes. They point to paper and thesis PDFs, vendor product pages, GitHub repositories and online-store book pages, and some PDFs are third-party mirrors.

The scope is native-code decompilation theory and tooling. Its six projects are Hex-Rays, Ghidra’s decompiler, JEB, RetDec, rev.ng-c and jsdec, and its eight intermediate representations include LLVM IR, VEX, BAP, REIL, ESIL, Binary Ninja’s LLIL and VTIL. It is a reading list, not an index of game decompilations or reconstruction projects.

The repository holds only README.md, with no license file or contribution guide, and GitHub detects no license, so the list states no reuse terms. Linked papers, books and tools keep their own rights, and some listed decompilers are commercial products. An independent reading list.

name: tiny-dec
description_en: Zhuo Zhang's small educational decompiler for 32-bit RISC-V (RV32I) ELF files, written in Python to teach how decompilation works rather than to compete with production decompilers. Its 19 deliberately separate stages run from ELF loading, decoding and p-code lifting through SSA, stack, type, variable and range recovery to control-flow structuring and C output, and the CLI can stop at any stage to print that stage's intermediate result. The README also offers a Claude Code plugin whose AI tutor walks learners through the stages with quizzes and exercises.
description_zh: Zhuo Zhang 用 Python 编写的小型教学用反编译器，面向 32 位 RISC-V（RV32I）ELF 文件，目的是讲清反编译的工作原理，而非与生产级反编译器竞争。它把流程刻意拆成 19 个独立阶段：从 ELF 加载、指令解码和 p-code 提升，经过 SSA、栈、类型、变量和取值范围恢复，再到控制流结构化和 C 代码输出；命令行可在任一阶段停下，打印该阶段的中间结果。README 还提供一个 Claude Code 插件，其中的 AI 导师会结合小测和练习，带学习者逐个阶段学习。
requirements: Reviewed at commit 4f5f1e0 (2026-05-27), the repository's only commit; the package is version 0.1.0, and the repository's test and lint workflows passed on that commit. The README calls it a teaching tool, not a production decompiler: it handles RV32I only, and unresolved expressions stay in the output as raw<...> rather than being guessed. A live demo site at tiny-dec.zzhang.xyz shows the stages.

Input is an RV32I ELF file. The repository commits 13 C test programs and 39 RV32I builds of them (-O0 and -O2, PIE and non-PIE) under tests/fixtures, so no outside binaries are needed. Rebuilding them or compiling one's own C code needs clang, lld and LLVM with RISC-V support, installed locally or through the included Docker development image.

Requires Python 3.12+ and Poetry, and the loader leaves ELF parsing to pwntools; the README lists Ubuntu/Debian system packages, and a devcontainer is included. The AI tutor needs Claude Code and installs as a plugin from the repository's marketplace manifest; its skill files hold one lesson guide per pipeline stage.
MIT license (Copyright 2026 Zhuo Zhang). The 500-test count and the example outputs are the author's. The tutor is an AI teaching aid.

name: sead: a decompilation of Nintendo’s first-party C++ standard library
description_en: Decompiles sead, the C++ standard library that Nintendo statically links into its first-party games, covering containers, heaps, strings, math, file devices, threads, the game framework and graphics. Compile-time presets target the recent versions used by Breath of the Wild, Super Mario Odyssey, Splatoon 3, Tears of the Kingdom and Super Mario Bros. Wonder, and game decompilations such as Breath of the Wild pull it in as a submodule. Names come from debugging symbols and assertions in retail titles, and the README warns that many inlined and templated names are guesses.
description_zh: 反编译 sead，即 Nintendo 静态链接进其第一方游戏的 C++ 标准库，涵盖容器、堆、字符串、数学、文件设备、线程、游戏框架和图形等模块。编译期预设针对《旷野之息》《超级马力欧 奥德赛》《斯普拉遁 3》《王国之泪》和《超级马力欧兄弟 惊奇》所用的较新版本，《旷野之息》等游戏反编译项目以子模块方式引入它。命名来自零售游戏中的调试符号和断言，README 也提醒许多内联与模板函数的名称只是猜测。
requirements: The reviewed master commit (2026-10-11, no releases) derives from aboood40091/sead but targets newer sead versions. The README says several modules currently fail to build for Switch and points to a GitHub project page for progress; seadVersion.h adds a Super Mario Maker 2 preset and a custom feature set alongside the README’s list.

Building needs no game files. Checking accuracy needs the original sead, which ships only statically linked in games: the README advises legally owning a recent first-party title with debugging symbols, naming Super Mario Odyssey 1.0.0, Splatoon 2 up to 3.1.0 and the Nintendo Labo pilot build.

The README asks for a partially C++17-capable compiler such as Clang 3.9 or newer and CMake 3.10+. CMakeLists builds an object library only for the nin (nnSdk, Switch) platform and links NintendoSDK headers supplied by the host project, the old or new open-ead header repository depending on a migration option. The README also describes Wii U (cafe) sources and declares other platforms unsupported.

The README asks contributors to match non-inlined functions against the original assembly, tolerating only register-allocation or obviously harmless reordering differences marked NOT_MATCHING, and to undo inlining with help from pilot builds and assertions; MATCHING_HACK_NX_CLANG guards codegen hacks. The repository has no checker or progress data of its own, and CI only runs clang-format, so matching is checked in consumer projects.

No license file is present and GitHub detects none; the README says nobody outside Nintendo has sead’s source. res/ holds the decompiled primitive-renderer shader sources plus a 2 KB compiled Wii U shader binary that was updated alongside them. Nintendo’s games keep their own rights.

name: TeddyCloud: a self-hosted replacement for the Toniebox cloud
description_en: Reimplements the Boxine cloud services a Toniebox talks to as a self-hosted C server, so the box can fetch audio, settings and over-the-air content locally while the owner controls what reaches the manufacturer. It serves and caches tonie audio, converts other audio into the box’s TAF format, can pass requests through to the original cloud, and adds a web interface, MQTT and Home Assistant integration. Protobuf definitions in the repository describe the box’s freshness-check, RTNL log and TAF header messages.
description_zh: 以可自托管的 C 服务器重新实现 Toniebox 所连接的 Boxine 云服务，使盒子能在本地获取音频、设置和无线下发内容，同时由用户控制哪些数据发往厂商。它可提供并缓存 tonie 音频，把其他音频转换为盒子使用的 TAF 格式，可将请求透传到原云端，并提供网页界面、MQTT 及 Home Assistant 集成。仓库中的 protobuf 定义描述了盒子的 freshness-check、RTNL 日志和 TAF 头部报文。
requirements: Reviewed at the stable master head of 2026-08-25, the v0.7.0 merge; release tc_v0.7.0 was tagged the same day, and active development continues on the develop branch. The project’s setup guide covers Toniebox 1 boxes with CC3200, CC3235 or ESP32 chips, and the README lists Toniebox 2 support as planned.

Setup is invasive and specific to each box: the project guide has owners dump their own box’s client certificates, flash a replacement CA into the box and redirect its DNS, and the server can extract or inject certificates in an ESP32 firmware dump. The repository ships no box certificates, firmware or tonie audio (those directories are empty placeholders). The dev-sandbox’s pre-generated certificates are self-signed and meant only for local testing.

Builds with a hand-written Makefile, protoc-c and a C toolchain, plus submodules for CycloneTCP/SSL/Crypto, cJSON, Opus, Ogg, the teddycloud_web frontend and emsdk; Linux debug builds enable AddressSanitizer and UBSan, and Docker is the recommended path on macOS. Release tc_v0.7.0 attaches an amd64 zip from the Windows/Linux release workflow, and Debian, Ubuntu and Alpine Docker images are published for several platforms. Stream conversion uses ffmpeg.

Python API tests for the custom-tonie JSON endpoints and a WASM TAF-encoder test run through Makefile targets; the reviewed workflows build and publish without running them. A dev-sandbox serves mock tonies, box and TAF data. Behavior with real boxes and the Boxine cloud remains project-reported.
GPL-2.0 (LICENSE); the vendored Cyclone stack, Opus, Ogg, cJSON and FatFs keep their own terms. Tonie audio, box firmware and Boxine’s services keep their own rights.

name: Reverse Engineering Reading List
description_en: A short reading list, compiled by One Thawt mostly in 2015–2016, of about 58 links to reverse-engineering tools, books, papers, talks and blog posts, kept in a README and a separate malware-analysis page. Sections run from disassemblers and debuggers, beginner talks and classic books through data-structure recovery papers, instruction-set references, iOS, Android and Windows material, unpacking, deobfuscation and protocol inference from network traces.
description_zh: 由 One Thawt 编写的简短阅读清单，主要成形于 2015–2016 年，在一个 README 和单独的恶意软件分析页面中收录约 58 个链接，涵盖逆向工程工具、书籍、论文、演讲和博客文章。各部分从反汇编器与调试器、入门讲座和经典书籍，到数据结构恢复论文、指令集参考资料、iOS、Android 与 Windows 相关资料、脱壳、反混淆，以及基于网络流量的协议推断。
requirements: Reviewed at commit a1ee767 (2023-05-02). 46 of 53 commits date from 2015–2016; the last added entries are x64dbg (2017), Binary Ninja (2018) and Ghidra (2019), and the 2023 commit merged a 2018 pull request that removed a dead link. The list therefore predates most current tools and research.

Most entries are a bare link, some followed by a quoted publisher or project description, and there are no notes on difficulty, platform or currency. Many point to 2010–2016 posts and PDFs on personal or project sites, and the README suggests archive.org for links that are down. Six of the 59 unique URLs in the two files gave no response, a 404 or a sign-in page, and the TIE and HyperV entries link to unrelated documents (an iOS 6 security talk and an IR-synthesis slide deck).
Books link to Amazon store pages, and IDA Pro, Binary Ninja and Hopper are commercial products. The Windows section also links older write-ups on kernel-protection bypasses.

GitHub detects no license and the repository has no license file, so the list states no reuse terms; linked works keep their own rights. The author offers copies of unavailable documents on request through a personal contact page.

name: Animal Forest: an in-progress matching N64 decompilation
description_en: Rebuilds the Japanese Nintendo 64 release of Animal Forest (Dōbutsu no Mori) from C code reverse-engineered from the ROM, combined with assets and assembly extracted from a user-supplied ROM. Default builds compare the uncompressed and recompressed ROMs with stored MD5 checksums. The README rules out use as a port base or for commercial purposes, and decomp.dev reported 18.52% of code matched at the reviewed commit.
description_zh: 将从 ROM 逆向得到的 C 代码与从使用者自备 ROM 中提取的素材和汇编结合，重建日版 Nintendo 64《动物之森》（どうぶつの森）。默认构建会用仓库保存的 MD5 校验未压缩与重新压缩的 ROM。README 明确该项目不作为移植基础，也不用于商业目的；decomp.dev 报告所审提交有 18.52% 的代码已匹配。
requirements: README calls this a work-in-progress decompilation whose codebase could change drastically and warns that some parts of the ROM may not yet be shiftable. The only configured version is jp, the Japanese N64 release, in both the Makefile and CI. The output is an N64 ROM; README states that the project is not a port and that serving as a port base or any commercial use is explicitly a non-goal. The GameCube Animal Crossing decompilation it links to is a separate project.

Supply your own Japanese Animal Forest ROM as the base ROM in baseroms/jp; .z64, .n64 and .v64 files are accepted. make setup decompresses it and checks the result against baseroms/jp/checksum.md5, then make extract uses splat to derive assembly and assets locally. The reviewed tree holds no ROM, graphics or binary asset files; game-derived content is limited to tables such as the DMA file table header and small address tables under src/objects.

README documents Linux, preferably Debian or Ubuntu, with make, Git, build-essential, clang, MIPS binutils and Python 3 with pip and venv; make venv installs pinned splat64 0.24.0 plus spimdisasm and mapfile-parser. The tools Makefile downloads static recompilations of IDO 5.3 and 7.1 from decompals/ido-static-recomp v1.2 and pigment64 0.6.3, and the build compiles libultra from the bundled ultralib subrepo. NON_MATCHING builds turn the checksum comparison off.

With COMPARE at its default, make rom and make compress check both ROMs against the stored MD5 values. Functions not yet decompiled remain extracted assembly included through GLOBAL_ASM. CI builds jp in a private container that supplies the base ROM and compiler archives, compares warning counts and uploads an objdiff-format report. decomp.dev's report for the pinned commit lists 465,796 of 2,515,744 code bytes (18.52%) and 2,998 of 14,415 functions matched, with no unit complete.

README licenses src and include, as far as possible, and other files that state no other license under CC0-1.0, excluding subrepos such as asm-differ, asm-processor, fado and ultralib. Nintendo's game, ROM contents and the downloaded compilers keep their own rights.

name: Remade
description_en: The source repository of remade.wiki, a community-curated directory of open-source reimplementations of closed-source software, mostly creative, productivity and engineering applications. Each listing is a YAML record naming the original software, languages, platforms, license and self-reported status, compatibility and limitations, and the directory also tracks requests for software nobody has reimplemented yet.
description_zh: remade.wiki 的源码仓库。remade.wiki 是由社区整理的目录，收录闭源软件的开源重新实现，以创意、办公和工程类应用为主。每个条目是一份 YAML 记录，注明被重现的原软件、编程语言、平台、许可证，以及自报的开发状态、兼容程度和局限；目录还收集尚无人重新实现的软件请求。
requirements: A young directory: the repository was created on 2026-10-09, and its history reached 308 commits by the reviewed commit of 2026-10-19. Its catalog files hold 123 project records, 13 supporting tools, 2 suites and 379 Project Requests for software with no listed reimplementation yet; remade.wiki is built from these files.

Listings target closed-source originals, mostly desktop and web applications, with Adobe, Autodesk and Microsoft products frequent among them. By category there are 53 creative, 37 productivity and 22 engineering records, plus 5 operating-systems, 3 developer-tools, 2 other and 1 games record. Status and compatibility are self-reported: 78 records are experimental, 26 alpha, 13 beta, 5 stable and 1 planned, and 107 claim partial compatibility.

POLICY.md requires independently authored code without leaked or unauthorized source, binaries or assets, excludes forks, ports, launchers and mods of the original, and leaves clean-room claims to each project’s authors; Remade states it does not audit provenance or legality. Only one record mentions a clean-room process.

The repository’s MIT license covers the directory’s code and data; listed projects keep their own licenses, from MIT and Apache-2.0 to GPL and AGPL, with one recorded as Unlicensed. The project’s own 2026-10-17 documentary audit of 119 entries left unreachable repositories and license conflicts unresolved and disclaims software, legal or compatibility certification.

name: PixMob IR reverse engineering: controlling event wristbands at home
description_en: Recovers enough of the infrared protocol used by PixMob event wristbands to light them at home, starting from Flipper Zero recordings made at concerts and games and replaying them to bracelets. Pulse-timing analysis found 38 kHz signals with bit intervals of roughly 700 µs, and targeted brute forcing from an ESP32 discovered hundreds of colour, fade, random and motion-mode commands, now sent through Arduino, Python and web tools. The README calls the result far from exhaustive and points to a later repository that decoded most of the full IR protocol through MCU dumping.
description_zh: 从在演唱会和球赛现场用 Flipper Zero 录下的信号出发，把录音重放给手环，恢复出足以在家中点亮 PixMob 活动手环的部分红外协议。脉冲时序分析发现信号载波为 38 kHz、比特间隔约 700 微秒；项目再用 ESP32 做有针对性的暴力枚举，找到数百条颜色、渐变、随机和体感模式命令，现可通过 Arduino、Python 和网页工具发送。README 称这些结果远未穷尽，并指向一个后来通过 MCU 转储基本解出完整红外协议的仓库。
requirements: Reviewed at the 2026-02-06 main head; there are no releases. The write-up covers IR bracelets, while the rf folder adds 915 MHz and 868 MHz OOK recordings and notes for RF wristbands, where a further encoding layer and a likely CRC remain unresolved. The project reports testing six IR bracelet versions made between 2014 and 2021, and a hardware table lists boards and MCUs where known.

Needs the user’s own PixMob bracelets with fresh batteries and an Arduino-compatible board or ESP32 with a 940 nm IR emitter, using the IRremote or IRremoteESP8266 library; a Flipper Zero can instead send codes from a separate repository. The Python tools need pyserial, PySimpleGUI and clipboard, and the web interface runs in Chrome and connects directly to the Arduino.

The evidence is recordings and observed bracelet reactions: the repository holds raw Flipper IR captures from several events, edited RF captures, the discovered effect definitions, a record of brute-force attempts and a dump of one bracelet’s 24C02 EEPROM. The README says brute forcing targeted only a few packet lengths, so the code list is far from exhaustive, and the programming and choreography signals used at events remain undiscovered.
Python unit tests cover the conversion functions and Flipper-file parsing; there is no CI. Effects are reported by the author and contributors from their own bracelets.
MIT (LICENSE). PixMob’s hardware, firmware and trademarks are outside that license, and the X-ray images are credited to Samy Kamkar.

name: Reverse Engineering resources (wtsxDev)
description_en: A single-README awesome list, started in January 2017 and maintained under the KaliTut name, of 139 reverse-engineering links in 16 sections: books, courses, practice targets, hex editors, binary-format tools, disassemblers, binary analysis, bytecode analysis, import reconstruction, dynamic analysis, debugging, Mac decryption, document analysis, scripting, Android and YARA. Entries are mostly a tool or resource name with its link, a few with a one-line usage note, and lean towards Windows and macOS tooling and malware analysis.
description_zh: 以单个 README 维护的 awesome 清单，2017 年 1 月创建，以 KaliTut 名义维护，共收录 139 个逆向工程链接，分为 16 个部分：书籍、课程、练习目标、十六进制编辑器、二进制格式工具、反汇编器、二进制分析、字节码分析、导入表重建、动态分析、调试、Mac 解密、文档分析、脚本、Android 和 YARA。条目大多只有工具或资源名称及链接，少数附一行用法说明，内容偏重 Windows 与 macOS 工具以及恶意软件分析。
requirements: Reviewed at commit b254985 (2019-03-07), still the default-branch head; all 26 commits date from 2017–2019, so the list predates most current tools and any LLM-assisted workflow. 24 of its 147 unique URLs gave no response, a 404 or a 503, among them every tuts4you download link, the Apple man-page links, Crackmes.de, malwr.com and the CodePlex z3 page.

Entries state no license, platform, maturity or maintenance status, so each tool must be checked at its own source; several, such as IDA Pro, 010 Editor and Binary Ninja, are commercial. Books mostly use amzn.to short links, and the header image and five closing links point to book lists on kalitut.com.

The Practice section places crackme and CTF sites next to public malware-sample repositories with only a warning to be careful with malware, and the Mac Decrypt section names tools without describing their use.

A package.json and .travis.yml set up remark-lint checks for list order, duplicate links and dead links on Node.js 8 under Travis CI. GitHub detects no license, the repository has no license file and the package.json license field is empty, so the list states no reuse terms; linked tools and books keep their own.

name: Decomp Academy
description_en: A free, English, in-browser course in matching decompilation maintained by Jack Price-Burns: learners read a function's target assembly, write C, and the original console compiler grades the result byte for byte. Lessons build from reading registers and arithmetic through control flow, structs, floating point, the ABI, globals, optimizer behaviour and 64-bit integers, then finish with functions adapted from open-source decompilation projects. The curriculum now spans GameCube PowerPC, Game Boy Advance Thumb and Nintendo 64 MIPS courses, and the frontend source is on GitHub.
description_zh: 由 Jack Price-Burns 维护的免费英文在线课程，在浏览器中教授一致性反编译：学习者阅读函数的目标汇编，编写 C 代码，再由原版主机编译器逐字节评判结果。课程从读寄存器和算术运算讲起，依次覆盖控制流、结构体、浮点、ABI、全局变量、优化器行为和 64 位整数，最后以改编自开源反编译项目的函数收尾。课程目前包括 GameCube PowerPC、Game Boy Advance Thumb 和 Nintendo 64 MIPS 三门，前端源码公开在 GitHub 上。
requirements: Reviewed at frontend commit a21f9d0 (2026-09-23); the repository was first published in June 2026 and has had commits most months since. The README still describes a single GameCube course of 258 lessons, but the reviewed curriculum and the live site list 755 lessons in three courses: GameCube (263), Game Boy Advance (251) and Nintendo 64 (241), each in four tiers from warm-up to real functions.

Lessons run in the browser at decomp-academy.dev and the README says no signup is needed to start; an account stores progress. Grading compiles the learner's C with the original compilers and diffs it using objdiff: Metrowerks CodeWarrior GC/2.0 for GameCube and SGI IDO 5.3 for Nintendo 64 on the hosted backend, a separate AGPL-3.0 repository that the README says runs the CodeWarrior compilers under wibo, and agbcc built to WebAssembly in the browser for Game Boy Advance.

No game files are needed: the later lessons adapt functions from open-source decompilation projects the README credits (Star Fox Adventures, Pikmin 2, Metroid Prime, Mario Party 4), and targets are generated server-side from each lesson's reference C. This repository contains no compiler, and the backend README says it commits only wibo, not MWCC; for local development the README expects Node 18+ and a sibling Star Fox Adventures decompilation checkout that supplies MWCC and binutils, while .env.example says a fresh clone uses the hosted compile API by default.
The frontend is AGPL-3.0, which also covers modified versions run as a network service. A CLAUDE.md lesson-authoring guide for Claude Code is committed.

name: Phantom Hourglass: an early-stage matching Nintendo DS decompilation
description_en: Recreates C++ source for The Legend of Zelda: Phantom Hourglass by hand-decompiling its European and US Nintendo DS releases, using the dsd toolkit to delink code from a user-supplied ROM and rebuild the ROM. objdiff tracks matches function by function, and the default build compares the output ROM with a stored SHA-1. The work is at an early stage: decomp.dev reported 2.82% of code matched at the reviewed commit.
description_zh: 通过手工反编译，为《塞尔达传说 幻影沙漏》的欧版与美版 Nintendo DS 重建 C++ 源码：借助 dsd 工具集从使用者自备的 ROM 中拆分代码，再重新构建 ROM。objdiff 逐个函数跟踪匹配情况，默认构建会将输出 ROM 与仓库保存的 SHA-1 比对。项目仍处于早期阶段：decomp.dev 报告所审提交有 2.82% 的代码已匹配。
requirements: README marks the project as a work in progress that targets the European and American versions, with other versions possibly supported later; configure.py takes eur or usa. Decompilation covers the ARM9 program, its TCM modules and overlays, while docs/build_system.md says the ARM7 program is not decompiled. The output is a Nintendo DS ROM, not a PC port.

Supply your own decrypted base ROM for each version in extract/ as baserom_ph_eur.nds or baserom_ph_usa.nds, matching the SHA-1 values in extract/README.md; dsd then extracts code and assets from it locally. INSTALL.md calls a byte-matching ROM optional and requires the user’s own DS ARM7 BIOS file, matching one of two listed SHA-1 values, to produce one. README says the repository contains no assets or assembly; config/ does commit game-derived dsd delink, symbol and relocation tables for 65 modules per version.

INSTALL.md lists Windows (recommended) or Linux with Python 3.11+ and pip, GCC 9+, Ninja and pre-commit hooks; on Linux the Windows compiler runs through wibo by default, or Wine on request. configure.py downloads dsd v0.11.0, objdiff v3.4.0, sjiswrap v1.2.2 and wibo 0.6.16 from GitHub releases, and a Metrowerks mwccarm bundle (version 2.0/sp1p5 is used) from decomp.aetias.com.

The default ninja targets generate objdiff data, run dsd’s module and symbol checks and compare the built ROM with ph_eur.sha1 or ph_usa.sha1. CI builds both versions in a build container that supplies extracted files and the compiler, running the ARM9 link, objdiff report and checks but not the ROM hash. decomp.dev’s default usa report for the pinned commit lists 102,202 of 3,622,306 code bytes (2.82%) and 1,351 of 24,610 functions matched, with 28 of 190 units complete.
The repository carries CC0-1.0; that dedication does not cover Nintendo’s game, its extracted files, the BIOS or the downloaded Metrowerks compiler.

name: Kinoko: reimplementing Mario Kart Wii’s physics engine for exact ghost replay
description_en: Re-implements Mario Kart Wii’s physics engine in C++ as a command-line simulator, continuing stblr/Hanachan’s goal of perfectly accurate time-trial ghost replay. Each test case replays a recorded ghost through the engine and compares kart position, rotation, velocities, speed and checkpoint state frame by frame with a trace captured from the original game. It is a behavioural reimplementation of the physics only, not a matching decompilation, and has no graphical frontend.
description_zh: 以 C++ 将 Mario Kart Wii 的物理引擎重新实现为命令行模拟器，延续 stblr/Hanachan 的目标：完全准确地回放计时赛幽灵记录。每个测试用例让引擎重放一条幽灵记录，并逐帧将赛车的位置、旋转、速度向量、速率和检查点状态与从原版游戏采集的轨迹比较。它只在行为层面重新实现物理部分，并非一致性反编译，也没有图形前端。
requirements: README describes a C++ reimplementation of Mario Kart Wii’s physics engine aiming at perfectly accurate ghost replay. At the reviewed commit STATUS.md lists 55 time-trial ghost test cases, each marked synchronized for every frame; the latest GitHub release, 0.6 (2025-09-04), adds x86-64 Linux, macOS and Windows binaries of the simulator. Source comments name addresses in the original game, but nothing rebuilds its executable; README points to the separate riidefi/mkw matching decompilation for that.

Running needs the Race folder (the Common and course archives) from your own Mario Kart Wii disc, placed relative to the executable; the repository ships no game files, and README requires any contributed frontend not to distribute in-game assets. The committed samples are time-trial ghost files (.rkg) with per-frame .krkg reference traces that README says come from a custom vabold/mkw-sp build running the PAL release; such traces are verification data captured from the game, as is common for reconstruction projects.

README lists g++ 13.1 with C++23, ninja 1.3 and Python 3.6; configure.py generates the ninja build and compiles testCases.json into the binary suite file. CMakeLists.txt also exposes a libkinoko library target for embedding the engine in other C++23 projects. CI builds with GCC 14 on Ubuntu; the program is a command-line host with test and replay modes, and README says no GUI is planned.

kinoko test compares position, rotation, internal and external velocity, speed, acceleration, soft speed limit, race completion and checkpoint values with every .krkg frame by exact equality and reports the first desynchronized frame; kinoko replay checks whether a ghost finishes with the time in its .rkg header. CI runs the suite with runtime files fetched from a secret-configured URL and checks that STATUS.md is current. These are project-reported results.
LICENSE applies MIT (copyright vabold, 2022–2026) to the project; Mario Kart Wii and its game data keep Nintendo’s rights, and the bundled doxygen-awesome-css theme has its own license file.

name: OWASP Firmware Security Testing Methodology (FSTM)
description_en: A free English methodology, maintained by Aaron Guzman and published on GitBook, for security testing and reverse engineering embedded-device firmware. It is organized as nine stages: information gathering, obtaining firmware, analyzing the image, extracting the filesystem, static analysis of its contents, emulation, dynamic testing, runtime analysis and binary exploitation, with example commands for tools such as binwalk, unblob, FACT, EMBA, Firmwalker, QEMU and Ghidra. An October 2025 revision added C/C++ static-analysis tools, SBOM generation and a mapping to the OWASP IoT Security Verification Standard (ISVS).
description_zh: 由 Aaron Guzman 维护、发布在 GitBook 上的免费英文方法论，用于嵌入式设备固件的安全测试与逆向工程。全文分为九个阶段：信息收集、获取固件、分析固件镜像、提取文件系统、静态分析文件系统内容、仿真、动态测试、运行时分析和二进制漏洞利用，并给出 binwalk、unblob、FACT、EMBA、Firmwalker、QEMU 和 Ghidra 等工具的示例命令。2025 年 10 月的修订加入了 C/C++ 静态分析工具、SBOM 生成，以及与 OWASP IoT 安全验证标准（ISVS）的对应关系。
requirements: Reviewed at default-branch commit ec666e8 (2025-10-05). Most of the text dates from 2019–2020, with a 2022 EMBA/EMBArk update and an October 2025 revision that refreshed tool references, removed commercial ones and added the SAST, SBOM and ISVS sections; the published GitBook includes those additions. A feature branch adding ISVS requirement mappings by stage (June 2026) was not merged at review, and a shorter 2020 Chinese translation sits on the separate zhong-wen-fstm branch.

Its stated audience is security researchers, software developers, consultants, hobbyists and information-security professionals. It is a single long reference page of procedures and commands rather than a paced course, and it points to the OWASP IoT Security Testing Guide for hardware, wireless, network and user-interface tests outside firmware.

Following it needs the firmware image or the physical device under an authorized assessment; the methodology tells testers to choose acquisition methods by project objectives and rules of engagement and to follow local laws. Some stages assume hardware debug access and a chip programmer. Tools mostly run on Linux; the README links a preconfigured EmbedOS Ubuntu VM from 2020 and, for practice, deliberately vulnerable firmware such as OWASP IoTGoat, DVRF and DVID.
Licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 (License.md).

name: Awesome Android Reverse Engineering
description_en: An awesome list of Android reverse-engineering training, tools and resources started in 2023 by James Stevenson, with 92 one-line entries, 16 of them starred as great and up to date. It covers courses, videos and books; static analysis and deobfuscation, networking and Frida-based instrumentation, decompilers and malware analysis tools; documentation and case studies; CTFs and crackmes; obfuscation and anti-reversing; and a short firmware and kernel section.
description_zh: James Stevenson 于 2023 年创建的 awesome 清单，收录 Android 逆向工程的培训、工具和资源，共 92 个单行条目，其中 16 个以星标注为优质且较新的资源。内容涵盖课程、视频和书籍，静态分析与反混淆、网络分析与基于 Frida 的插桩、反编译器和恶意软件分析工具，文档与案例研究，CTF 与 crackme，混淆与反逆向，以及一个简短的固件与内核部分。
requirements: Reviewed at commit 0ade43d (2025-07-08). 51 of 58 commits date from 2023; a March 2025 rewrite reorganized the list and added the obfuscation and firmware sections, and the July 2025 commit removed the Cloud API section while its contents-menu entry remains.

Entries give a link and a one-line summary with no license, version or maintenance notes, and some summaries are loose; AFLSmart, for example, is described as a firmware-image fuzzer, while its own README presents an input-structure-aware greybox fuzzer. 8 of 90 unique URLs gave no response, a 404 or a 530: five linked GitHub repositories no longer exist, four of them (the ATDF, Paranoid, libhooker and Android kernel-exploits entries) added in the March 2025 rewrite, and the Houseparty case study, the Flare-On page and AndroidXref did not load.

Six entries are the maintainer's own tools and one his blog post. Burp Suite, IDA Pro, JEB and DexGuard are commercial, the Documentation section links the APKMirror and APKPure download sites, and tools for bypassing app controls, dumping memory and kernel exploitation appear as listed.

LICENSE is the MIT License (2023, James Stevenson), although the README points to a LICENSE.md that does not exist; placeholder changelog and to-do files from the repository template remain under .github. Linked tools, books and APKs keep their own terms. An independent discovery list.

name: Mario Kart: Double Dash!!: a matching GameCube decompilation of the debug build
description_en: A work-in-progress 1:1 decompilation of Mario Kart: Double Dash!! that rebuilds the GameCube main.dol of the US debug build (MarioClub_us) from C and C++ with the original Metrowerks compilers, checking it against a stored SHA-1. The build splits the binary from a user-supplied disc image, and objdiff compares objects during development. decomp.dev reported 47.09% of code matched at the reviewed commit; a European retail target is configured but marked as not working yet.
description_zh: 《马力欧卡丁车：双重冲刺!!》的进行中 1:1 反编译：用原版 Metrowerks 编译器从 C 与 C++ 源码重建美版调试构建（MarioClub_us）的 GameCube main.dol，并与仓库保存的 SHA-1 比对。构建从使用者自备的光盘镜像中拆分二进制，开发时用 objdiff 比对目标文件。decomp.dev 报告所审提交有 47.09% 的代码已匹配；欧版零售目标虽已配置，但标注为尚不可用。
requirements: README calls this a WIP 1:1 decompilation and says only the debug version is supported: the default MarioClub_us (USA) target, whose main.dol SHA-1 config/MarioClub_us/build.sha1 records. configure.py also lists Release_eu, but its config.yml is marked as not working yet, and CI builds only MarioClub_us. The output is a GameCube DOL, not a PC executable or port.

Copy your own disc image of that build to orig/MarioClub_us; ISO (GCM), RVZ, WIA, WBFS, CISO, NFS, GCZ and TGC images are accepted. README says the repository contains no game assets or assembly: decomp-toolkit splits the user’s DOL using the committed symbol and split tables, and during the build extracts a font, system.arc and build-time data from that DOL locally.

Builds need Python and ninja on Windows (native tooling recommended), macOS (with wine-crossover) or Linux (an automatically downloaded wibo on x86, Wine elsewhere). configure.py pins decomp-toolkit v1.6.2, objdiff v3.3.1, binutils 2.42-1, sjiswrap v1.2.1, wibo 0.7.0 and the 20250812 compiler bundle, using Metrowerks GC/2.6 for game, JSystem, MSL and TRK code and GC/1.2.5n for the Dolphin SDK libraries.

Objects marked Matching (518 in configure.py; 277 remain NonMatching and 13 Equivalent) are compiled from source, the rest are taken from the split DOL, and the build checks main.dol against build.sha1. CI builds MarioClub_us in a container that supplies the disc files and compilers, uploads a progress report and validates symbol order for changed C++ files. decomp.dev’s report for the pinned commit lists 1,517,644 of 3,222,748 code bytes (47.09%) and 8,695 of 15,357 functions matched, with 518 of 807 units complete.
